messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] How to include files when deploying an application
messages.body_plain:
Dominique,

Thanks for taking the time to try out the ShinyApps alpha. We really appreciate the help!

Any file that is part of your application will be uploaded to the ShinyApps service, and can be accessed from your ui.R or server.R files as you normally would with shiny or shiny-server. All files in the directory specified as the appDir parameter of deployApp() are considered to be part of the application. The appDir parameter defaults to the current working directory.

For example if you wanted to source a file called "functions.R", you would call source('functions.R') from server.R file. When you call deployApp(), all the files in the current directory will be uploaded and functions.R will be sourced when the application is finished being deployed. If you have tried this and seem to be having issues, please let us know.

I hope that helps, and feel free to reach out if you have further questions.

-Andy

Let me know if that helps.

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: trigger updates
messages.body_plain:
There are two problems with doing a (potentially) long-running, periodically scheduled task directly in an R Shiny app.

1) There is no guarantee that your Shiny app will be running all the time; by default, the Shiny Server application server shuts down R processes that are not being used.

2) R is single threaded, so while this scraping is being done, no other work can be done in that R process.

Ideally you would move the job into a separate R script, and have that script scheduled to run periodically. I don't think this is supported by ShinyApps.io at this time though.

Shiny does let you run scheduled tasks using time-based reactive primitives like invalidateLater, reactiveTimer, and reactivePoll. However, because of the above reasons, these are best suited for tasks that only need to run while the app itself is running, and can complete their task in a relatively small amount of time.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: SQL Backend?
messages.body_plain:
Alok,

As you pointed out, using SQLite may be a good option. However, I wanted to bring up a few points which are outlined in the Application Instances <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/blob/master/guide/guide.md#application-instances> section of the Getting Started Guide:

Files that are written to the local file system (such as SQLite database) of a running application are not persisted across deployments or instance restarts. In other words, if you were to re-deploy the application, the files that were written before you re-deployed, would be lost. Jin Rou,

The issue here is a known limitation of the ShinyApps platform. The rjags package requires the jags library to be installed on the system. The package fails to build because the jags library is not found. ShinyApps doesn't currently support installing OS packages, however we are planning on supporting this in the future. We've taken care to install a number of frequently used OS packages, but jags is not one of them. If there is enough interest, we can add it as part of the standard installed packages.

-Andy

library(ggplot2)

proj <- read.csv("245 Staph Database_251D.csv")

# Returns a logical vector of which values in `x` are within the min and max
# values of `range`.
in_range <- function(x, range) {
  x >= min(range) & x <= max(range)
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  limit_data_range <- function() {
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Because we're using reactiveUI for x_range and y_range, they start
    # out as null, then get resolved after the client and server talk a bit.
    # If they are not yet set, there will be some errors in this function, so
    # do nothing for now (this function will be run again).
    if (is.null(input$x_range) || is.null(input$y_range)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Limit range of data
    # Take a subset of the data, respecting the limited range
    proj_sub <- proj[in_range(hw[[input$x_var]], input$x_range) &
                   in_range(hw[[input$y_var]], input$y_range), ]

    proj_sub
  }

  output$main_plot <- renderPlot({

    # Take a subset of the data, respecting the limited range
    proj_sub <- limit_data_range()

    if (is.null(proj_sub))
      return()

    # Get the x and y values from the non-range-limited data, for convenience
    xdat <- proj[[input$x_var]]
    ydat <- proj[[input$y_var]]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Make the base plot

    # If any models are drawn, make the points less prominent
    if (input$mod_linear || input$mod_quadratic || input$mod_loess)
      point_alpha <- 0.5
    else
      point_alpha <- 1

    # Separate by sex, if requested
    if (input$sex) {
      aes_mapping <- aes_string(x = input$x_var, y = input$y_var,
                                colour = "sex", shape = "sex")

      # Use different point geom specification, depending on if we're separating
      # by sex.
      points <- geom_point(solid = FALSE, alpha = point_alpha)

    } else {
      aes_mapping <- aes_string(x = input$x_var, y = input$y_var)

      # Use different point geom specification, depending on if we're separating
      # by sex.
      points <- geom_point(shape = 21, alpha = point_alpha)
    }

    # Base plot
    p <- ggplot(proj_sub, mapping = aes_mapping) +
      points +
      theme_bw() +
      scale_colour_hue(l = 40) +
      scale_shape(solid = FALSE) +
      # # Show the original range
      scale_x_continuous(limits = range(xdat)) +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = range(ydat))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # If the range has been limited, draw lines displaying the limits

    if (max(input$x_range) != max(xdat)) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = max(input$x_range), linetype = "dashed",
                          alpha = 0.3)
    }
    if (min(input$x_range) != min(xdat)) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = min(input$x_range), linetype = "dashed",
                          alpha = 0.3)
    }

    if (max(input$y_range) != max(ydat)) {
      p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = max(input$y_range), linetype = "dashed",
                          alpha = 0.3)
    }
    if (min(input$y_range) != min(ydat)) {
      p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = min(input$y_range), linetype = "dashed",
                          alpha = 0.3)
    }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Add model lines

    if (input$mod_linear) {
      p <- p + geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE, size = 0.75,
                           linetype = "dotdash")
    }
    if (input$mod_quadratic) {
      p <- p + geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE, formula = y ~ x + I(x^2),
                           size = .75, linetype = "dashed")
    }
    if (input$mod_loess) {
      p <- p + geom_smooth(method = loess, se = FALSE, linetype = "solid",
                           span = input$mod_loess_span)
    }

    print(p)
  })

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create renderUI sliders for x and y range, because their limits
  # depend on the selected x and y variables.

  output$x_range_slider <- renderUI({
    xmin <- floor(min(proj[[input$x_var]]))
    xmax <- ceiling(max(proj[[input$x_vary]]))

    sliderInput(inputId = "x_range",
                label = paste("Limit range"),
                min = xmin, max = xmax, value = c(xmin, xmax))
  })

  output$y_range_slider <- renderUI({
    ymin <- floor(min(proj[[input$y_var]]))
    ymax <- ceiling(max(proj[[input$y_var]]))

    sliderInput(inputId = "y_range",
                label = paste("Limit range"),
                min = ymin, max = ymax, value = c(ymin, ymax))
  })

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Functions for creating models and printing summaries

  make_model <- function(model_type, formula, ...) {
    # Get the subset of the data limited by the specified range
    proj_sub <- limit_data_range()
    if (is.null(proj_sub))
      return()

    # In order to get the output to print the formula in a nice way, we'll
    # use do.call here with some quoting.
    do.call(model_type, args = list(formula = formula, data = quote(proj_sub), ...))
  }

  output$mod_linear_text <- renderPrint({
    formula <- paste(input$y_var, "~", input$x_var)

    # Use sex as a predictor variable
    if (input$sex) {
      formula <- paste(formula, " * sex", sep = "")
    }

    summary(make_model("lm", formula))
  })

  output$mod_quadratic_text <- renderPrint({
    formula <- paste(input$y_var, " ~ ", "I(", input$x_var, "^2) + ",
                     input$x_var, sep = "")

    # Use sex as a predictor variable
    if (input$sex) {
      formula <- paste(formula, " * sex", sep = "")
    }

    summary(make_model("lm", formula))
  })

  output$mod_loess_text <- renderPrint({
    formula <- paste(input$y_var, "~", input$x_var)
    summary(make_model("loess", formula, span = input$mod_loess_span))
  })

})
